text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-simplify-judge.md <<'EOF'
# Independent cross-judge

Choose candidate A as the base. It removes the assignment algorithm while retaining token-level recall for a misspelled first name inside a longer name. Candidate B identifies a real defect in its own global-vocabulary proposal. Candidate C loses the central `jahn` example against `John McDonnell` because whole-string distance counts the entire surname as missing text.

These are design scores on a five-point scale. They reflect source inspection, not executed query results.

| Criterion | A | B | C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| User-facing name recall | 4 | 2 | 1 |
| Code and migration simplicity | 4 | 3 | 5 |
| Score, rank, and limit correctness | 4 | 2 | 3 |
| Data-independent behavior | 5 | 1 | 5 |
| SQLx compile feasibility | 5 | 5 | 5 |
| Total | 22 | 13 | 19 |

A wins despite C's smaller query. C removes a behavior the user specifically wants. A requires SQL and Rust changes to use one corrected similarity consistently. Its static SQL is compatible in shape with SQLx macros, but compilation against the migrated schema still must establish actual parameter and result types.

B selects one correction from all candidate names. Adding another spelling can change which preexisting person qualifies. Its distance is also shared across all candidates, so retaining `PhoneticRank` misrepresents candidate-specific edit quality. Enumerating every global correction would introduce complexity without improving this base.

C's whole-string phonetic gate also treats the first segment of a full name as decisive. It loses omitted titles, middle names, surnames, and reversed token order. Those losses follow from its expressions and do not depend on a benchmark. Its defensive CASE and simple built-in bounded-distance call are useful independently of its whole-string design.

Graft B's adversarial data-independence test into A. Add a second qualifying spelling and confirm the existing person's score and eligibility remain unchanged. Compare eligibility before repository caps so the test does not confuse legitimate ranking displacement with a changed match rule. Retain A's existing canonical-plus-alias CTE shape, which B independently recommends.

Graft B and C's `levenshtein_less_equal(query_word, candidate_word, 1)` into A's guarded token comparison. A only needs to distinguish zero, one, and greater distances. Preserve A's CASE around the call, which C also explicitly requires. Do not graft C's whole-string gate or helper/index removal.

The current source confirms that the primary-person gate runs before fallback in `exposed/src/lib/domain/services/entity_search.rs`. It uses both empty member results and `has_qualifying_individual`, then appends fallback after primary results. The service deduplicates funders and applies the remaining shared funder allowance. Preserve these branches while replacing rank comparison. Repository ordering, alias winner selection, the service merge, and LIMIT must all use corrected similarity in the same direction if A's rank change is adopted.

A introduces a fallback threshold that the old fallback did not have. The old member adapter admits a non-null `person_name_distance`; 0.8 only governs primary search. A's new threshold is coherent with corrected-query search, but it is a behavior change. Confirm it is covered by the user's simplification request and state it in the final result. Do not describe A as preserving every former fallback match. Test omitted words and word permutations against the real database before choosing expectations.

A also deliberately removes one-to-one occurrence assignment and distance-first ordering. Preserve the original query word order, allow each word to choose its candidate correction independently, and retain deterministic ID and canonical-before-alias tie breakers. Replace algorithm-specific assertions with repository behavior checks, including a case where score ordering changes which result survives LIMIT.

Watch A's unmatched-word rule. It retains an unmatched token and lets trigram scoring decide admission. That can admit some names with unmatched tokens at a low strictness or sufficiently similar long text. A token over 255 characters is safe from a fuzzystrmatch exception because of CASE, but it is not necessarily rejected if left unchanged and subsequently accepted by word_similarity. Distinguish the safety requirement from any explicit oversized-input rejection contract.

Keep the frozen regression corpus unchanged for the initial verification run. Investigate changed outputs before considering an expectation change. Add explicit live repository or HTTP checks for `jahn`, `jahn mcdonnell`, a titled John name, unrelated tokens, Jonathan, punctuation-only input, length boundaries, individual aliases, canonical tie preference, primary person suppression before the limit, primary organizations first, deduplication, and the combined funder cap.

All candidates correctly preserve the already applied migration. A has the smallest forward migration because only `person_name_distance(text,text)` disappears. Its down migration necessarily retains the old function body as historical rollback code. Verify the new migration against existing rows and perform down/up in an isolated populated database. No repository edits or query execution were performed for this judgment.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Wrote [independent judgment](/tmp/exposed-simplify-judge.md).

Choose A. Scores are A 22/25, B 13/25, C 19/25. Graft bounded `levenshtein_less_equal` and B’s data-independence regression test.

C breaks `jahn` against full names. B makes existing matches depend on unrelated vocabulary additions. A’s new fallback threshold and score ordering need explicit behavioral verification. Keep the frozen corpus unchanged during the initial verification run.
